conclusions: All four lateral failed trials explicitly logged joint effort limit before subsequent safety-output loss of support; sweep-y test-level height failure alone is an incomplete description.
left050-y caught FL_hip at -26.80286113 Nm in the first FAULT diagnostic, exceeding 26.07 Nm; other trials did not record the triggering joint or peak.
No sampled pre-fault WBC solve failure, infeasible residual, or NMPC unhealthy flag was found. This does not prove absence of every inter-publication transient.
Sampled projected hip targets remained well inside the +/-0.65 rad locomotion cap; no sampled hip-clamp boundary was reached.

These logs do not identify the unique cause of the requested-effort overshoot. Delay, gain changes, phase/command changes, and policy/plant tracking must not be promoted from candidates to proven root causes.
The result is simulation evidence only, not real-hardware torque calibration or locomotion acceptance.

initial_run_summary: Forward/backward +/-0.15,0.30,0.50 m/s and yaw +/-0.5,1.0,1.5 rad/s completed all six-second phases and final 30-second stance without a controller fault
Lateral +/-0.15 m/s completed; +0.30 m/s faulted in the initial sweep and independent -0.30,+0.50,-0.50 m/s attempts also faulted during acceleration
All four lateral failures logged joint effort limit before subsequent loss of height under safety output; one captured FL hip request was -26.80286113 Nm versus 26.07 Nm safety threshold
Backward -0.50 m/s and yaw -1.5 rad/s did not pass the strict governed-reference equality check; stability and tracking are reported separately
Backward -0.50 m/s minimum 100 Hz truth height was 0.310164 m, close to the unchanged 0.31 m acceptance floor

test_harness_versions.difference: V2 adds --direction for independent attempts, default both unchanged. After all runs, the current harness adds a ROS-shutdown check before marking completion; completed phase durations in all saved runs were independently checked, so previous outcomes are unchanged

limitations: One initial run per axis plus three independent lateral attempts; short six-second stages do not establish endurance or a maximum safe hardware speed
NMPC, reference generation, WBC task weights and task-space PD were not retuned
Unreached levels after a safety failure remain untested, not failed or passed
Script reports full-body-frame mean velocity; offline pose derivatives independently report yaw-only heading-frame velocity
Script tracking mean-error tolerance is max(0.10 m/s, 40 percent of command), yaw max(0.20 rad/s, 40 percent); RMSE is reported, not a pass criterion
Raw logs remain ignored; pose post-check is 100 Hz and inferred command budgets approximately 10 Hz, not a hardware-boundary trace

Kinematics mode labels reuse throttled diagnostics and can lag FAULT; active-pose extrema may include post-fault falling samples. Fault timing analysis separates these consequences from pre-fault support
No full-rate torque trace, evaluated NMPC desired-height trace, or gain/delay/friction ablation was captured, so the effort-overshoot root cause is not uniquely identified
Timing/sensor/friction assumptions are not identified hardware models; no serial devices or physical motion were used

repeatability.interpretation: The initial x sweep completed its stability checks; rebuilt-x later failed at +0.5 m/s. Preserve both results. No ablation isolates binary content, asynchronous solver timing or other trial-to-trial variation; a changed binary hash alone is not proof of the failure cause.

negative_lateral_0_3.rebuilt_independent_result: 6 s motion and 30 s final stance completed; raw stability/tracking passed
negative_lateral_0_3.interpretation: The same requested -0.3 m/s direction/speed has both fail and pass records. It is not established as consistently reliable; do not describe all fast lateral trials as failures or assign the difference to binary content without an ablation.

negative_forward_0_5.result: 6 s motion and 30 s final stance completed; raw stability/tracking passed
negative_forward_0_5.interpretation: The independent -0.5 m/s trial passed but its minimum height was only about 8.1 micrometers above the configured lower guard. Passing this run is not evidence of a wide stability margin.

conclusions: rebuilt-x and rebuilt-y sweeps, plus independent rebuilt-left050-y and rebuilt-right050-y, explicitly logged joint effort protection while truth body height was above 0.31 m; subsequent height failure follows safety retreat.

rebuilt-x completed signed 0.15 and 0.30 m/s phases, then failed +0.50 m/s after 4.828 simulation seconds. The initial sweep-x completed stability checks at signed 0.50 m/s; both observations are retained.
rebuilt-y completed signed 0.15 m/s phases, then failed +0.30 m/s after 2.424 simulation seconds. Independent -0.30 m/s has an earlier failed trial and a later fully passed trial.

Independent rebuilt-back050-x at -0.50 m/s and rebuilt-right030-y at -0.30 m/s completed their 6 s moving phases and 30 s final stances with raw stability/tracking passed. Do not characterize every higher-speed signed motion as failed.
Independent lateral +0.50 and -0.50 m/s failed after 1.692 and 1.492 simulation seconds respectively. Both launch logs show effort protection before the reported height-guard failures.

No saved pre-fault Trot diagnostic in the four final failed trials shows WBC failure, QP constraint-residual failure, NMPC unhealthy status or a projected hip target at the +/-0.65 rad cap. These sampled checks do not exclude inter-publication transients.

No final rebuilt failure captured an effort-threshold crossing in the throttled joint diagnostic. An earlier left050-y trial did capture FL_hip=-26.80286113 Nm exceeding26.07 Nm; do not apply that identity to other trials.

A sampled send-time budget below the limit does not exclude requested-effort overshoot when a delayed packet evaluates PD against newer physical feedback. No unique cause is established, and changed binary hashes alone do not identify the cause of trial variation.
These results are simulation observations only, not calibrated physical motor torque, RK3588 timing evidence, or real-hardware motion acceptance.

summary: Requested Kp 60/60/90 and Kd 2.0 are applied to stand-up, stand settling, MPC_STANCE and TROT; static stand compensation was recalculated
Overall simulation acceptance failed; the requested gains are not demonstrated robust at all tested speeds
Forward/backward +/-0.15 and +/-0.30 m/s completed in both initial and postbuild runs; initial +/-0.50 completed, but postbuild +0.50 triggered joint effort protection at 4.828 s
Postbuild independent -0.50 m/s backward completed with mean heading vx -0.476159 m/s and minimum height 0.310008 m; the 0.31 m height-guard margin was extremely small
Yaw +/-0.5,1.0,1.5 rad/s completed in both runs and final 30-second stance; strict reference tracking did not pass at -1.5 rad/s

Lateral +/-0.15 m/s completed in both runs; +0.30 and +/-0.50 m/s failed with effort protection. Initial independent -0.30 failed, while its postbuild independent repeat completed with mean heading vy -0.309071 m/s; high-speed results are not uniformly reproducible
No torque limit, effort safety threshold, height guard, NMPC Q/R, WBC task weight, or task-space PD was relaxed for these tests
